scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8879: Users in both pods report that no internal portal
loads by NAME anymore -- web0.local through web3.local all fail with
name-resolution errors. Loading a portal directly by its IP address (e.g.
http://10.200.0.3) still works, and pings to 10.200.0.2 succeed. Diagnose.

injection.action: stop the BIND (named) DNS service on dns_server

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: dns_server BIND (named) DNS service
Mechanism: the named daemon on dns_server (10.200.0.2) has been killed, so
  nothing answers on port 53 and every *.local lookup from the pods times
  out -- which is why the portals fail by name. Everything else is healthy:
  the host 10.200.0.2 itself is up and pingable, the OSPF path works, and
  the web servers keep serving HTTP (portals load when addressed by IP).
  The symptom is purely dead name resolution.
Localization: dns_server
Root cause: named not running on dns_server (port 53 closed)
Fix: `systemctl start named` on dns_server
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart the BIND DNS service on dns_server (e.g. `systemctl start named`).
Once named is answering again, web0.local..web3.local resolve to their
10.200.0.x addresses and the portals load by name. The web servers and the
network need no change.
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: BIND/named DNS service down (name resolution dead, port 53 closed)
bonus-rules-out-network: notes 10.200.0.2 is reachable and portals load by IP, so the network and web servers are healthy -- only resolution is broken

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** The `named` (BIND 9.18) DNS daemon on `dns_server` is the failed subsystem. The daemon is completely absent from the process table and no socket is bound to UDP/TCP port 53 on any interface.

**Mechanism:** Both client hosts (`host_1_1_1_1` and `host_2_1_1_1`) are correctly configured to use `10.200.0.2` as their sole nameserver — the right address for `dns_server`. When they issue DNS queries for `web0.local` through `web3.local`, the packets reach `dns_server` (ICMP/IP reachability is confirmed healthy), but nothing is listening on port 53. UDP DNS queries receive an ICMP port-unreachable response or simply time out, causing resolvers on both hosts to return `no_addresses` for every `.local` hostname. Because name resolution fails before a TCP connection is even attempted, the HTTP client immediately aborts (curl exit code 000), explaining the portal failures. Direct-IP access bypasses the resolver entirely and therefore still works.

**Localization:** Solely `dns_server` (`10.200.0.2`), specifically the `named` process and its port-53 listener. The nft ruleset contains only Docker-internal NAT chains — port 53 is not blocked by any firewall rule — ruling out `dns_port_blocked`. Web servers are healthy (HTTP 200 on localhost). L3 routing to and from `dns_server` is fully intact.

**Root cause:** The `named` daemon on `dns_server` is not running, leaving port 53 unbound and all DNS queries unanswered.

**Fix:** Start (or restart) the `named` service on `dns_server`: `service named start` (or `named -c /etc/bind/named.conf`). Once the daemon is up and the zone files for the `.local` domain are loaded, all four web hostnames will resolve and portal access will restore automatically.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly localizes the fault to dns_server (10.200.0.2) and names the named daemon as the failed subsystem.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-component: BIND/named DNS service down (name resolution dead, port 53 closed)
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies the BIND (named) daemon on dns_server as absent and port 53 unbound, matching the expected diagnosis of DNS service down and name resolution failing.

per_axis.axis: bonus-rules-out-network: notes 10.200.0.2 is reachable and portals load by IP, so the network and web servers are healthy -- only resolution is broken

Proposes starting/restarting the named (BIND) service on dns_server, which matches the expected fix to restore DNS resolution.
